Chapter 9: Reframing the Narrative — Strengths, Creativity, and Growth.
Imagine what could happen if ADD, or ADHD, wasn't just seen as a set of obstacles, but as a completely different way of being in the world. When you start to look at it from this angle, something powerful shifts. Suddenly, you’re not just focused on what’s hard—you're also noticing your strengths and opening yourself up to real growth.
Let’s talk about spotlighting strengths for a moment. So many people with ADD or ADHD are natural innovators. They spot connections that others might miss, and their quick thinking, adaptability, and enthusiasm can really light up a room—or drive a creative project forward. The trick is to find spaces and teams that truly value these qualities, and then to lean into them on purpose. When you do, you’ll be amazed at what you can bring to the table.
Now, let’s dive into the idea of a growth mindset. If you believe your abilities can grow with effort, practice, and the right kind of support, that changes everything. Suddenly, mistakes aren’t proof that you’re failing—they’re stepping stones for learning. This kind of outlook encourages you to experiment, keep going when things get tough, and, maybe most importantly, show yourself a little compassion along the way.
There’s another big idea here—redefining what success actually means. It’s not about fitting into a mold or checking the same boxes as everyone else. For some, success comes from chasing creative hobbies, starting a business, or forging a path in an unconventional career. For others, it’s about building deep relationships, or giving back to the community. The point is, your path doesn’t have to look like anyone else’s.
And here’s something that really matters—sharing stories. When you hear from people who’ve walked this road and found their own ways to thrive, it’s incredibly inspiring. These real-life stories show just how many ways there are to succeed, and they remind us that none of us are truly alone in this journey.
If you take one thing from this chapter, let it be this: reframing the narrative around ADD or ADHD isn’t just possible—it’s a pathway to discovering your strengths, unlocking your creativity, and growing in ways you may never have imagined.
